sourceClaims.label: The report reviews extensions/pi-claude-marketplace/index.ts and its mirrored tests/index.test.ts owner.
The entry-point owner suite is one of the strongest suites in the historical sweep.
The suite proves the documented NFR-2 containment routes with throwing cwd and notification collaborators, including both notification-failure levels.
Registration is checked with exact strong-mock expectations for event, command, and tool names and explicit per-case verification.
The registration cases contain no It.isAny, anyTimes, or hidden verification.
Hydrate, reconcile, recompute, and aggregate order is behaviorally discriminated by ordered cwd reads and stage-specific side effects.
The only remaining entry-point issues are two type-safety/documentation gaps rather than behavioral defects.
index.ts creates a double-cast placeholder ExtensionContext solely for registerHooksBridge's over-broad options type.
registerHooksBridge does not consume opts.ctx and should drop or narrow that field so the placeholder can be removed.
The resources_discover registration retains an unexplained as unknown as bind cast and should use the direct overload or document the concrete type-system obstacle.
The default extension factory documentation explains await ordering but not what registrations the factory installs.
The factory documentation should add a leading what-clause while retaining its DISP-01 rationale.
tests/index.test.ts was historically classified clean.
All other index.ts behavior, including catch discipline, aggregation spread safety, and session-start handling, was historically classified clean.
The historical report ran no typecheck, lint, test, or coverage command.
The historical resources_discover cast finding was explicitly unverified without a typecheck rerun.
tests/edge/notification-boundary.ts was used as context but not reviewed as its own target.
The report reviews the two shared concern modules and their two mirrored owner tests.
Both shared concern pairs were historically classified clean, with soft-dep called exemplary.
soft-dep.test.ts runs the complete 2x2x2x2 runtime truth table as sixteen sibling cases.
Every soft-dependency row has a matching descriptive title and whole-array handwritten expectation.
hooks.test.ts covers each appendHooksBlock union arm and distinguishes absent from empty lenient matchers.
softDepMarkers is hermetic because SoftDepStatus is an explicit plain-data input and no node_modules probe runs in the pair.
The global npm-root integration-test risk belongs to platform/pi-api and not to shared/concerns/soft-dep.ts.
shared/concerns/hooks.ts is distinct from the hooks bridge and its other references do not replace owner behavior coverage.
Only two minor production-style findings remained in hooks.ts.
Both shared-concern owner tests were historically listed as clean.
appendHooksBlock uses an explicit union-with-undefined parameter where an optional parameter was preferred.
Changing appendHooksBlock entries to an optional parameter preserves explicit undefined calls and requires no caller changes.
ClaudeHookEvent and HookSummaryEntry semantics are documented in a detached implementation-note block rather than adjacent JSDoc.
The public hook type documentation should be split into adjacent JSDoc blocks while retaining its rationale.
soft-dep.ts was historically classified clean because it is pure, explicitly injected, documented, and contains no unsafe assertions.
The historical review did not cover the platform/pi-api soft-dependency probe implementation.
The report reviews sixteen shared production modules and their sixteen mirrored owner tests, excluding notify and concerns.
The shared-core area was historically classified as the cleanest area in the sweep.
Error classes and path errors are asserted by class identity, structured fields, cause-depth bounds, and cycle behavior.
atomic-json tests compare complete bytes in case-owned temporary directories.
The classifier owner tests use exhaustive one-row-one-case tables.
path-safety.test.ts exercises parent escapes, symlink positions, unreadable fallback, and traversal order with real temporary filesystems.
completion-cache.ts exposes a test-only reset over module-scope mutable Maps and should be converted to factory-owned state.
session-env.ts and debug-log.ts contain process-global dependencies, while getPluginIndex inconsistently bypasses its clock seam.
A fixing pass should prioritize factory-owned completion-cache state before the smaller clock and environment items.
The cold plugin-index case uses a timestamp-format regex that would accept a wrong but well-formed instant.
getPluginIndex should use its injected now function for persisted timestamps so the owner can assert an exact independently derived instant.
Two completion-cache unlink-error cases assert only Error identity and code-not-ENOENT rather than the exact error code.
The unlink-error cases should assert the exact deterministic failure identity or code rather than a negative condition.
After factory ownership replaces resetCompletionCache, its owner case should prove isolation between two cache instances.
markers.test.ts repeats negative truncation and padding assertions after exact equality already proves the complete constants.
The redundant marker negative assertions should be removed.
notify-context.test.ts tests four exported entrypoints as flat cases instead of one describe group per entrypoint.
The notify-context owner cases should be grouped once per exported function for readability.
resetCompletionCache has no production caller, explicitly exists for tests, and clears two module-level Maps shared across cases.
Completion-cache state should move behind a factory object threaded from composition, after which the reset export should be deleted.
getPluginIndex uses new Date instead of its existing injected now function at both persisted timestamp writes.
applySessionEnv mutates process.env and the historical report proposed a defaulted environment parameter for tests.
hookDebugLog reads process.env internally and the historical report proposed a defaulted environment parameter for tests.
The remaining thirteen shared-core owner pairs were historically classified clean.
The historical report excluded notify and concerns and ran no test, lint, typecheck, or coverage command.
